rules.label: 40% self-pay discount for uninsured patients not approved for financial assistance
rules.quote: All uninsured patients receive a 40% Self-Pay discount on their account balance at the time of billing.

rules.label: Charity write-off for verified out-of-state Medicaid balances
rules.quote: Patients with verified Medicaid out of state balances in which it is not feasible for AVRMC to complete an application with the out of state Medicaid intermediary will be considered indigent and all balances adjusted off as "Charity."

eca_not_before.quote: The patient shall not be billed prior to 46 days after discharge.

notes: Policy effective for dates of service on or after September 1, 2022.
Screening must occur within 45 days of date of service or discharge for uninsured patients.
Patients may apply up to three months prior to receiving service; eligibility valid for one year after determination.
AVRMC will attempt to contact discharged patients at least once a month for six months regarding financial aid screening.
Verbal decline is not valid for opting out; signed Opt Out Form required.
If patient requests hospital cease contact, AVRMC documents request and records it.
If AVRMC exhausts contact efforts and patient does not respond in 182 days, lack of cooperation considered informed decision to decline screening.
Hospital's right to pursue collection of personal injury, liability, workers' compensation, or fault-based insurance not limited.
Charity write-off may not apply to balances prior to September 1, 2022; to be determined by hospital management.
If third-party coverage discovered later, financial assistance write-off reversed and third-party insurance filed.
Application process same as required for CICP or HDC applicants.
Policy references Colorado Indigent Care Program (CICP) and Colorado Hospital Discounted Care Act (HDC).
Exhibit A flowchart for HDC process referenced but not included in text.
Co-Insurance and Payment Arrangement policy referenced for patients who opt out but not detailed.
Good faith estimates provided to uninsured patients but no payment requested until opt-out or denial.
Patient notification requirements: posting Patient Rights on website, in waiting areas, providing copy at registration, including notification on billing statements.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Proved: every Colorado resident at or below 250% of the poverty line qualifies for help under this policy's written rules.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts

findings.title: Ignores assets for Colorado-protected households

law.quote: THE METHODOLOGY MUST NOT CONSIDER A PATIENT'S ASSETS.

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, savings and assets never changes the outcome.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts (pairs of households)

findings.title: Doesn't require a Medicaid application first

law.quote: DENY DISCOUNTED CARE ON THE BASIS THAT THE PATIENT HAS NOT APPLIED FOR ANY PUBLIC BENEFITS PROGRAM

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, whether they applied for Medicaid or other public programs never changes the outcome.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts (pairs of households)

findings.title: No collection lawsuits or garnishment before day 182

law.quote: NO MEDICAL CREDITOR COLLECTING ON A DEBT FOR HOSPITAL SERVICES SHALL ENGAGE IN ANY PERMISSIBLE EXTRAORDINARY COLLECTION ACTIONS UNTIL ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY-TWO DAYS AFTER THE DATE THE PATIENT RECEIVES HOSPITAL SERVICES.

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: If the first bill goes out on day 46 after care (Colorado allows bills from day 46), the policy's written timeline allows collection actions from day 46. Colorado law bars them until day 182.
